cards.text: God has just spoken the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:1-17), and the people trembled and stood at a distance while Moses, Israel's leader, approached the thick darkness where God was (Exodus 20:18-21). Now the LORD gives Moses a message for the Israelites. They've seen for themselves that He spoke to them from heaven.

cards.question: God has spoken to the Israelites straight from heaven. What does He say they must not make for themselves?

answers.text: a king to rule over them
a tower that reaches the sky

cards.text: What the Israelites ARE to make for God is an altar of earth. On it they sacrifice their burnt offerings and peace offerings, from their sheep, goats and cattle.

cards.question: God says He will come to the Israelites and bless them only at Mount Sinai.
If the Israelites build God an altar of stones instead, what would shaping the stones with a chisel do to it?

cards.text: One more altar rule: the Israelites must not go up to God's altar on steps, so that no one's nakedness is exposed on it.

Then the LORD gives Moses ordinances for everyday life: when servants go free, what's owed when someone is hurt or an ox gores, and how to repay for stolen animals, grazed fields and burned grain. It includes the famous rule of eye for eye, tooth for tooth, and the death penalty for crimes like murder and kidnapping.

cards.question: God tells the Israelites how to treat people from other lands who live among them. Why must the Israelites never oppress them?

answers.text: the Israelites were foreigners in Egypt

cards.question: God says that if a mistreated widow or orphan cries out to Him, He will surely hear their cry.

cards.text: This one's heavy, friend. Then God says, "My anger will be kindled, and I will kill you with the sword; then your wives will become widows and your children will be fatherless."

cards.question: If an Israelite lends money to a poor man among God's people, God says he must not act as a creditor or charge him ___.

cards.text: If an Israelite takes his neighbor's cloak as collateral, he has to give it back by sunset. Picture a friend holding your phone until you pay back that twenty, except he has to hand it back before dark, and you STILL owe him the twenty.

cards.question: Why must an Israelite return his neighbor's cloak by sunset?

answers.text: the neighbor needs it for worship
keeping it overnight brings a curse

cards.text: And God says that if that neighbor cries out to Him, He will hear, "…for I am compassionate."

God goes on: the Israelites must not blaspheme God or curse the ruler of their people, and they're to give Him the firstborn of their sons, cattle and sheep. Then He says, "You are to be My holy people."

Then God turns to the courtroom: no spreading a false report, no joining the wicked as a malicious witness, and no following the crowd in wrongdoing. You know when the whole group chat piles on somebody and you hit the thumbs up just to keep the peace? NOT in court, friend.

cards.question: In a lawsuit, God tells the Israelites to show favoritism to a poor man.
If an Israelite comes across his enemy's stray ox or donkey, God says he must ___ it to him.

cards.text: And if an Israelite sees the donkey of someone who hates him fallen under its load, he can't just leave it there; he has to help. Yes, friend, even for the guy who takes your parking spot every single morning.
Back in court: don't deny justice to the poor, stay far away from a false accusation, and don't kill the innocent or the just, for God will not acquit the guilty.

cards.question: God tells the Israelites not to accept a bribe. What does He say a bribe does?

cards.text: Then God comes back to foreigners: the Israelites must not oppress them. They know how it feels, because they were foreigners in the land of Egypt.

cards.question: For six years the Israelites sow their land, but in the seventh year they let it rest. What does God say that rest is for?

answers.text: so the poor can eat from it
so the priests can harvest it

cards.question: God says the seventh-day rest is for the Israelites' ox and donkey too.
After all those laws, God tells the Israelites to pay close attention to everything He's said. Then what must never be heard on their lips?

cards.text: Three times a year, the Israelites are to celebrate a feast to God: the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Harvest and the Feast of Ingathering. For Unleavened Bread, they eat unleavened bread for seven days at the appointed time in the month of Abib.

cards.question: Why is the Feast of Unleavened Bread held in the month of Abib?

answers.text: God gave the law that month
the manna first fell that month

cards.question: God says the Israelites may come before Him empty-handed at the Feast of Unleavened Bread.

cards.text: Three times a year, all the Israelite males are to appear before the Lord GOD. Then come a few offering rules, like not letting the fat of God's feast remain until morning.

cards.question: What part of their firstfruits do the Israelites bring to the house of the LORD?

cards.text: And one last rule: don't cook a young goat in its mother's milk. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this teaching isn't done.
